[h1] The Amazingly Fun Soulslike Experiment of your Dreams [/h1] 

[b]If you truly enjoy the actual gameplay of the Souls series, you will love this game.[/b] This series has consistently been popular thanks to its great combat mechanics, exciting gear loadouts, and powerful boss challenges. All of these really shine here.

Joining the core gameplay loop this time are 3 exciting additions:
1. The ability to play entirely different builds easily without needing another huge lengthy RPG playthrough.
2. A new highlight on consumable items, because the gameplay is session-based and they are plentiful.
3.  Unique character-specific abilities that serve as the backbone of your specific strengths.

[u] Which Elden Ring players will not like this game? [/u]
a) Players who are used to over-leveling or over-upgrading their weapons before facing bosses.
b) Players who are used to looking at a guide to find guaranteed spawn locations for overpowered equipment.
c) Players who are used to steamrolling bosses 3v1, rather than 3v1 being the evenly designed fight this time around.

This game plays like a dev's passion project. It is so fun.

Despite that it's a p fun action rogue-lite with combat ripped from Elden Ring (which is all they really had to do) with a pretty big map with a lot of content, though it can get a little repetitive after a lot of runs but things like invasions and shifting earth can help alleviate that. Hope it gets more support and content in the future cuz it's a very solid base to build off of and has infinite potential IMO.

I do not often leave reviews, but I felt a positive one was needed here because too many people are leaving poor reviews for the wrong reasons.

If you are on the fence about Nightreign, do not be swayed by negative reviews on account of it being "too hard", or "unfair". The sheer number of players who skipped every tutorial screen is abundantly clear. Players who do not aim for flask upgrades, do not itemize for the run or even their OWN character. Hell, I know my own friends did not know how their own abilities worked.

The toxic part of the community who have loudly prided themselves on not using summons or consumables are the same part of the community bashing their head against the wall run after run, without considering how they should change their approach. They believe the game should change its approach instead. They are the same people who complained about Radahn, and later his being nerfed.

Ignore them.

----------------------------------

Now, why I recommend Nightreign. 

It is a delightful genre blend of two genres that seem insoluble, and Fromsoft has made a vinaigrette. It encourages you to actively try new builds that are out of your comfort zone, creates tense moments of fighting against the clock where triumph feels damn good, the bosses and their OSTs are fantastic, and you are drip fed game depth that keeps things exciting. ABOVE ALL, Nightreign accomplishes what so many hero based games fail these days: the characters feel wildly unique and are all a blast to play.

This may be an opportunity for inner-company growth for the next generation of devs, but it doesn't feel like someone's homework. This is a love-letter to Fromsoft's catalogue that leaves me eager to see what the next generation will do with stories we love.

[b]TL;DR[/b]: i have a weirdly large amount of feedback for a game i like so much. the devs listened to the community the first months and addressed main complaints (duo runs, increased difficulty, new mode, tougher boss variants, lots of QoL updates) but the game will no longer receive content and that's very sad, seeing it's missing so little to become so much better. the one remaining gripe it’s also the biggest one for me: the relic system. it’s still a gachaslop that needs a rework to let us craft the relics we need or at the very least reroll specific passives and colors of each relic.

it has only gotten [i]more complicated[/i] (Murk and Deep relics) while at the same time becoming increasingly more important at higher difficulties. i could literally buy thousands of relics hoping to get a combination i like, but that just turns into reading and selling hundreds upon hundreds of items with random, often-contradictory passives and colors. it's really more of a slot machine than it is progression and, for me at least, that just doesn’t work or is enjoyable at all.

so, here are my two cents on how it could be improved:
[list]
[*] [b]crafting[/b]: break unwanted relics into components to [i]build[/i] a target relic (choose color + a couple of guaranteed passives for both regular and Deep relics).
[*] [b]rerolling passives[/b]: reroll passives [i]individually[/i] (and/or the color) one at a time, with an escalating Murk cost. this way we could venture into high-difficulty runs against Everdark Sovereigns with confidence that we’ll be getting materials to build the exact relics we want. high risk, high reward; ideally deterministic and a 0% gacha/randomness system that doesn’t waste player time
[/list]

The perfect game for whoever wants to enjoy the Elden Ring gameplay without having to play a whole 50h run. Don't get too intimidated by the mixed reviews, the game is fun, and a rather good multiplayer experience from a studio which isn't very good at it. It's a nice side product to expand the "Souls" franchise, and I hope it will encourage FromSoftware to explore other genres with the same intent.

However, you shouldn't get the game if :

- You want to play something like Elden Ring : the play any other soulslike. Nightreign only has the skin of Elden Ring, it is the complete opposite experience. No time to fool around and explore, in Nightreign, you pick a direction and go there fast. There is no losing time, no farming to compensate death, and luck will be as important as playing well.

- You don't have friends to play with and won't play with randoms : you don't need 2 friends, 1 friend and a random can work well. Solo will only be enjoyable if you know the game well and you have good skill at this kind of game, because you are very weak at the start of a run. I hope they'll add a 2 players mode, and adjust the solo play correctly too, right now it only works for three players.

- You expect something more than gameplay : this is not Elden Ring, this is a roguelike. You will play dozens, hundreds of hours if and only if you like the gameplay enough to do the same thing over and over. If not, you'll get bored quickly.

This is Elden Ring: Boss Battle Royal. 

Its a neat idea but I don't think it works when you break down what a souls-like is. The entire match is summarized as one long "corpse run" until you can try to fight the Night Lord boss at the end again. That's 30 minutes of scrounging for resources so you can try and learn more of the boss's moves this time.

The content in-between that end, is repetitive and static. 

The game is not intuitive for cooperative play.  Markers on map is the only way to communicate.  No chat, voice, or ping system.  Duo's are not implemented, solo is a non-balanced joke, coordinating three friends together is hard.

I feel the game is too fast paced. It is a sprint to try and accumulate resources before the next stage. 

This game is NOT friendly to players who have not familiarized themselves with the previous game. If you loved the first game, you may enjoy this. If you've never heard of the first game, I cannot recommend Nightreign.

it's good but has minor issues across the entire board that add up to a bigger problem with the game altogether . It needs improvements in optimization, impact of leveling up, weapon variety, skill variety, map variety, better damage scaling for players and enemies, the circle closing speed, more interesting buffs, and more enemy variety. There also isn't any duos or crossplay but duos is getting fixed

+ The game provides a very fun fast-paced gameplay, similar to Battle Royale style games.
+ Classes have, while simple, still interesting abilities, which don't get in the way of other gameplay features.
+ All the encounters are fairly balanced. Nevertheless, it would be nice to have a newer variety of enemies.
+ Level design is challenging and requires you to swiftly make strategical decisions.
+ Character design and stories are unobtrusive, but still enjoyable
+ Some features you didn't even think about (like after-expedition route overview) add nice flavour and make you look at games under new angles.

- The weapon upgrade system feels unnecessary and underwhelming
- 2-player co-op is missing
- Rememberance expeditions realistically cannot be done in parties.
- While the ping system is made pretty well, there's still room for improvement. For example, sound and visual ques should be more obvious.

Both voice and text chats feel completely unnecessary, since first and foremost it leaves out the toxicity the community brings. Moreover, ping system is more than enough for clear communication

So basically everything the devs presented is in the game and works very well.
